Plasma vitamin E kinetics
Vitamin E absorption gives an estimate of how much of consumed vitamin E is available to the body. The dual isotope method to
measure fractional a-tocopherol absorption is based on the ratio of the plasma concentrations of the administered oral a-tocoph-
erol to IV (equals 100%). Using this technique, fractional a-tocopherol absorption in healthy women is 55%  3% (mean  SEM;
n ¼ 10) (Traber et al., 2019b). Higher fractional absorption (80%) has been estimated using radioactive tocopherol with the
balance method (oral minus excreted) (Novotny et al., 2012). Dietary fat (40% vs. 0% fat in the meal) had no effect on a-tocoph-
erol absorption. However, when labeled a-tocopheryl acetate was used as the test dose, fat was necessary for absorption (Bruno
et al., 2006). These data suggest that vitamin E esters in food or supplements should be consumed with a fat-containing meal
for optimal absorption.
